subject: Memory issue during fitting a CFA

messages.author: 362d8fa923280412
messages.subject: Memory issue during fitting a CFA
parts:
Hi!

My recent project has a need to fit a CFA model with one latent variable and do regression between the latent and 360 predictors (please see the attached syntax). The code worked completely fine when I set the mechanism to deal with missing value "missing=ML" (the attached Word file).

However for other following analysis I have to set this setting to be "missing=listwise".


I went to used a cluster with 256GB RAM and tried the same program. The computation run for an hour and then gave me a more serious error.

Besides, from the report of the cluster computation, the program had  consumed 180GB RAM before this error.

Why the mode of dealing missing value could lead to such influence and why is this program using such huge storage?

Please kindly give your suggestions if you know any information!! Thanks!!!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Memory issue during fitting a CFA
parts:
I am confused: when did you get those memory issues? When you ran cfa()
with missing="ML", or when you ran cv_regsem()?

In case of the former (when running cfa()), would it be possible to send
me the data (or a snippet of the data, just enough to reproduce these
issues)? Then I will investigate.

In case of the latter, you will have to contact the authors of regsem.
Another option is to look at the lslx package.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Memory issue during fitting a CFA
parts:
Thanks for the example. The memory bomb is caused by the computation of
the 'Gamma' matrix (=N times the ACOV of the sample statistics). For
this setting, the matrix is just too large.

But you don't need it, and you shut if off by using the NACOV = FALSE
argument:

fit5 <- cfa(model = Model5, data = dat, missing='listwise',
orthogonal=TRUE, std.lv=TRUE, verbose = TRUE, NACOV = FALSE)

Yves.

messages.author: 362d8fa923280412
messages.subject: Re: Memory issue during fitting a CFA
parts: Thank you Prof Rosseel for you helpful suggestions! I was finally able to run the computation with setting in below:

orthogonal=TRUE, std.lv=TRUE, verbose = TRUE, NACOV = FALSE, se='none')

Best,
Mianxin
